score.band_label: The largest single-round gain W1-15 has recorded, and the minimum is carried by an item the round did not touch

status_reasons: min-over-axes is 2.0 against a wave-1 gate of 7.0, carried by RI-CRM02 (faction crime and writs), untouched for three rounds — crime.writs is initialised, serialised and deserialised and pushed to nowhere in game/src.

The round's own headline claim, that only render/interior.js and sim/stealth/system.js decide what a room is lit by, is false: render/places.js draws writ-house and barge-hold — the game's opening two rooms — from its own private lamps, and writ-house disagrees with its own simulation over 71 of 154 floor cells.

The light term is clamped at L = 1.0000 over 12,210 of 16,996 indoor floor cells at noon clear, so over roughly seven-tenths of the province's indoor floor it decides nothing. Standing rather than new: round 3 measured 11,800.

biggest_gap.what: On the round's own 16,996-cell chest-height grid over all 115 interiors, 12,210 cells (71.8%) read L = 1.0000 at noon clear and 10 rooms are entirely flat at 1.0000. Under round 3's flat 0.04 ambient the same lamps give 11,800 (69.4%) and 7 flat rooms, so this is a standing defect of the LAMP SCALE and not a regression introduced by this round's ambient — the derived ambient costs 2.4 percentage points at noon clear and 0.3 at 03:00. The round measured the same defect at ROOM granularity and published it as '11 of 115 rooms are flat at noon', which is the same fact one order of magnitude too small. The four-arm comparison: round 3's flat 0.04 gives 69.4% and 7 flat rooms, round 4 derived at noon clear 71.8% and 10, at noon overcast 71.1% and 10, at 03:00 overcast 69.7% and 7, and the round-3 critic's arm-01 control at 0.75 gives 94.4% and 63. archon-apothecary is 50 of 50 cells at L = 1.0000 with an ambient of 0.2264 in a 9.83 x 4.98 m room with 8 lamps.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: RI-STL01 §3's bar is that light decides whether you can be seen, and over seven-tenths of the province's indoor floor a player standing anywhere reads the same maximum L, so there is nowhere indoors to hide.

remedy.action: Re-derive authored_intensity_to_L_scale and reach_m in game/data/stealth/detection.json on the JOINED corpus, exactly as this round re-derived window_daylight_k. RI-STL01 §3's 'within 4 m of a flame' (L 0.60) and '4-9 m from a flame' (L 0.25) rows were transcribed against rooms that applyInteriorBounds() now shrinks to a fifth of their declared area, so the same scale that reads 0.60 at 4 m in a 13.6 x 15.6 m shop saturates a 9.83 x 4.98 m one. Then add the SATURATED-CELL FRACTION to tools/harness/w1-15-r4-lights.mjs's discrimination table beside mean_spread, because a room with one dark corner and forty-nine clamped cells currently scores as discriminating.
remedy.acceptance: On the same 16,996-cell chest-height grid over all 115 joined interiors, fewer than 40% of cells read L >= 0.9999 at noon clear, and no more than 3 rooms are entirely flat — against 71.8% and 10 today. The delete-the-fix control must bring 71.8% back.

other_gaps.what: engine.js#cellFor() at 5394-5398 routes barge-hold, writ-house, helstrom-market, stormhold-street and rootlands-well to render/places.js, which builds point lights from its own private lamp() helper with hardcoded Three.js intensities and never imports world/interior-lighting.js. barge-hold and writ-house ARE records in game/data/world/interiors/, so syncInteriorLights() lights them from the shared policy while the player looks at a room that policy has never seen. writ-house: 2 drawn point lights plus a DirectionalLight the file calls 'the only daylight in the room', against 1 simulated synthesized fail-open hearth 5.22 m away, and 76 of 154 floor cells disagreeing, 71 of them drawn lit and simulated dark (47 of 108 on a 1 m-inset grid). barge-hold: 2 drawn at hardcoded positions against the record's own 3, brightest sources 3.80 m apart, and the drawn hold is 7 x 12 m against the record's 7 x 16 m. These are the first two rooms of the game (engine.js:3420). writ-house is also on this round's own list of eleven rooms the shared fail-open is rescuing — and it is the one of the eleven that does not get it.
other_gaps.remedy: Either route those two ids through render/interior.js, or have render/places.js build its lamps from litLights(rec) and its window from windowPlan(rec). Then add all five cellFor() ids to tools/harness/w1-15-r4-lights.mjs's denominator so the next round cannot miss them.

other_gaps.what: tools/analysis/w1-15-consumption.mjs's VACUITY section names, for six parameters, the world-side producer that must fill the collection their reader indexes, and exits 1 if it is missing. readersOf(producer) is a NAME SEARCH over game/src outside harness/. On a staged copy where syncCoverVolumes() still exists, is still called from the fixed step, and returns an empty list, all six rows PASS and the tool exits 0 — against a world in exactly the state the round-3 critic graded 0. The tool's --control falsifier only ever tests an ABSENT NAME, never an INERT PRODUCER, which is RULES.md 6's 'inert control'.
other_gaps.remedy: Make the guard read the collection rather than the producer's name: import the sim, run one fixed step in a fixture interior, and assert the collection is non-empty. The tool already has the browser-free machinery to do it; the check is three lines and a fixture record.

other_gaps.what: This round found Engine.getGuardBand() was a second implementation of the guard ladder reading the raw bounty total, and fixed it to read attributedIn(). engine.js:9074 (_questPlayerView) sums Object.values(crime.bounty) with no unattributed subtraction and feeds it, through dlgMovableTerms at engine.js:9020 and _talkPersuader at engine.js:2987, to disposition.js:313 — `const bountyTerm = -G.fDispCrimeMod * Number(player.bounty || 0)` with fDispCrimeMod = 0.02. The round's own D4 scenario, 680 g across four unidentified reports at guard band 0, therefore costs -13.6 disposition with every person in the province. justice.json's promise is scoped to guards and the guards are correct, so this is not a broken promise; it is the same rule-10 shape one module over, unlooked-for.
other_gaps.remedy: Give CrimeWorld a single attributedTotal() and route _questPlayerView, the HUD field at engine.js:4129 and getSanctionState's deepKinRegard/factionConsequences through it, so there is one definition of 'what the world can pin on you' rather than four.

other_gaps.what: interiorAmbientL() clamps at CANOPY_DAY_L and reports clamped: true 'so a census can count how many rooms are sitting on the ceiling'. Because DAYLIGHT_K is pinned so the brightest room reads exactly 0.30 at sky 1.0, raw > ceiling is unreachable: 0 of 115 rooms can set that flag on the shipped corpus. It is a guard for a future join, which the header says, but it is currently a flag that cannot be raised and a reader should not mistake 'no rooms clamped' for evidence.
other_gaps.remedy: Either say so at the field, or pin k on a percentile of the aperture distribution rather than the maximum, which makes the clamp a live invariant instead of a dormant one.

corpus_extended.note: §3's light table gives L for 'a torchlit interior' and 'unlit' and says nothing about how many lamps a room may hold before the sum of them saturates. Two rounds have now calibrated a scale against its two torchlit rows and neither could see that 69-72% of the province's indoor floor sits at the top of the resulting scale, because the item offers no per-CELL discrimination requirement — only per-room language. The item needs a stated floor: what fraction of an interior's floor must be below flame_near for the room to count as lit rather than washed out.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and deliberately so. (1) The brief's item 3 asked for a frame-time number or a plain statement that the ruling stands unmeasured; the first attempt was killed by its own timeout at load 7.54 per core and the outcome of the retry is recorded in §10. (2) RI-QST05 was not re-measured and its 3 is inherited. (3) RI-CRM02 rests on one spot-check. (4) tools/run-all.mjs and the 29-assertion stl-live.mjs were not run — both launch many browsers and the box was over its instance ceiling for most of this run. Everything in §§1-7 was taken offline, with no browser, before any browser work began.
